structure_flags.label: lem:collision-uniform-modulus
structure_flags.one_line: The proposal's declared novel kernel is a supporting lemma rather than a root theorem/proposition/OEQ solve target; elevate the modulus itself to a theorem and make estimation and confidence results consequences.

novelty_flags.label: prop:collision-identification
novelty_flags.one_line: Its all-moments identification claim is already Theorem 5.4 of VirkMazaheriWu2026; retain it only as background or an explicitly collision-focused corollary with genuinely additional content.

novelty_flags.label: prop:homogeneous-reduction
novelty_flags.one_line: Its population homogeneity characterization duplicates VirkMazaheriWu2026 Proposition 6.2; it should be reduced to a corrected sanity corollary, not presented as a research result.

novelty_flags.label: tldr / novelty_justification / comparator_promise_table
novelty_flags.one_line: The prose claims a strict advance over VirkMazaheriWu2026, but no root statement formally states the strict comparison on a common class; add an explicit theorem contrasting the separated VMW procedure with the quotient-law procedure, or soften the prose to 'informed by'.

soundness_flags.label: symbol V(P) versus def:compressed-operator
soundness_flags.one_line: The symbol definition gives the row space of [M₀ᵀ,M₁ᵀ], which lies in R^(2d_z), whereas V(P) is declared d_x×k; use the row space of the vertical stack [M₀;M₁], as in the construction and VMW.

soundness_flags.label: prop:homogeneous-reduction
soundness_flags.one_line: Although ΔQ=τ⋆I and νP=δτ⋆, W1(ν̂n,δτ⋆)=∫|x−τ⋆|dν̂n is not generally the absolute error of aᵀΔQc; that equality requires a separately enforced one-atom estimator or a different scalar estimator.

soundness_flags.label: ass:reference-proxy-separation
soundness_flags.one_line: The condition invokes potential outcomes, but the cited VMW assumption is Z ⟂ (X,Y) | (T,U); the proposed stronger potential-outcome version is not the cited standard condition.

soundness_flags.label: ass:target-proxy-separation
soundness_flags.one_line: The cited VMW condition is X ⟂ (Y,T) | U, not X ⟂ (Y(0),Y(1),T) | U; weaken it to the published observable-outcome condition or retag and justify the stronger condition.

soundness_flags.label: ass:bounded-record
soundness_flags.one_line: VMW finite-sample regularity bounds X, ZXᵀ, and YZXᵀ, whereas this assumption bounds Z and both potential outcomes separately; the stated 'bounded VMW moment contributions' tag is not the cited condition.

soundness_flags.label: ass:gap-window
soundness_flags.one_line: VMW spectral separation requires distinct effects, not the local two-sided window g/2≤δ(P)≤2g; retag this as a local-asymptotic regime definition and justify it.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: All rate and confidence statements
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Claims are conditional on known fixed k,d_x,d_z and the bounded, uniformly positive, uniformly conditioned VMW class M; they make no unknown-order claim.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Uniform root-n and local-minimax statements are only over the displayed fixed-parameter class M (and M(g)); no tier cap beyond this stated conditional regime.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: PROTECT consumer
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: The finite-fitness/censoring bridge from PROTECT to the VMW observed-moment model is expressly not proved here.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The proposal makes no patient-level, hazard-level, or clinical-validity claim until a separate bridge theorem is supplied.

The paper exists at the claimed venue and presents synthetic sampling through higher-order multilinear observable moments to identify causal mixtures.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv:1807.07237v2 corroboration; journal primary version not inspected
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The work studies Gaussian location mixtures and projects estimated moments to a truncated moment space before recovery, with Wasserstein guarantees; it is a repair-method comparator rather than a VMW result.
The paper studies adaptive honest confidence sets under Wasserstein loss for density estimation over Besov smoothness classes.

Align the proxy-independence and boundedness assumptions with the exact VMW conditions, and label the g-window as a justified local-asymptotic regime rather than a VMW standard assumption.
